sources.description:
Quad leaders’ summit in Philippines is Trump’s first, as Australia joins US and Japan to protect AI technologies in face of China’s efforts to dominate

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Anthony Albanese will attempt to walk a tightrope in his relationship with Donald Trump when the two leaders meet on Tuesday, as Australia signed on to a US-led pact to secure the technologies ​and critical infrastructure for artificial intelligence supply chains.

The Quad leaders’ summit in the Philippines’ capital of Manila will be Trump’s first, in either of his presidencies. The US president, fresh from a crushing midterms result, will take centre stage in gatherings of Asian leaders and prepare for historic three-way talks with Xi Jinping of China and Russia’s Vladimir Putin this week.

sources.title: Proposed NSW laws to allow coalmine to increase production pose ‘serious corruption risk’
sources.description:
Bill to authorise expansion at Mount Pleasant coalmine, subject to a landmark high court decision, will be debated this week

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

A New South Wales government bill to increase coal production at a Hunter Valley coalmine creates a “serious corruption risk” for the state due to a clause that would give the resources minister “king-like” powers, the barrister and anti-corruption campaigner Geoffrey Watson says.

The state parliament will this week debate legislation to allow MACH Energy to increase coal production at the Mount Pleasant mine in Muswellbrook by 32% to 16.5m tonnes per year.

sources.title: Birth keeper told mother of baby who later died to ‘go home and rest’, NSW inquest hears
sources.description:
Sita Kali was involved in care for two of four babies who died between 2022 and 2024 in Lismore after free births or home births

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A self-described birth keeper advised a pregnant woman whose baby later died to “go home and rest” after she was given urgent medical advice to present to an emergency department, the New South Wales coroner’s court has heard.

Sita Tara Kali was involved in the care of two of four babies born in free births or home births who died in the northern rivers region between 2022 and 2024. An inquest into the deaths began in the Lismore local court on Monday. The families of the four babies were not present.

sources.title: NSW halts new law to crack down on underquoting by real estate agents at 11th hour
sources.description:
Backdown is one of several premier Chris Minns has announced in recent weeks as state prepares for election in March

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The Minns government has mothballed laws intended to protect homebuyers from underquoting after the premier said real estate agents in his Sydney electorate had raised concerns about their effect amid a housing market downturn.

Changes due to come into effect on Tuesday would have banned agents in New South Wales from lowering the advertised price of a property beneath a written offer previously rejected by a seller, with fines of up to $110,000 or three times an agent’s commission, whichever was greater.

sources.title: Monday briefing: The many stages of the UK-EU relationship – and what’s next
sources.description:
In today’s newsletter: From situationship to a possible makeup, a look at the evolving relationship, and the bloc’s big feelings about the future

Good morning. Ahead of the hotly anticipated UK-EU summit this Friday, Andy Burnham is expected to make the reset of our relationship with Europe the pivotal theme of his white-tie speech at the lord mayor’s banquet in London tonight.

The prospect of closer ties – and the possibility of going “all the way” to reversing Brexit – has been met with jubilation and relief in some quarters and vehement opposition in others, while around Westminster and across the media the psychodrama has been spiralling for weeks.

UK news | A woman who alleges she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity to campaign for a staggered age of consent, which would make it illegal for adults over a certain age to have sex with 16- and 17-year-olds.

Youth unemployment | Andy Burnham has pledged to intervene as early as childhood to tackle youth unemployment before a watershed review, promising “a root-and-branch rethink of how we support childhood in the modern world”.

Environment | The strongest El Niño in centuries has added urgency to UN climate talks in Turkey as vulnerable countries face “compounding” crises. In other Cop31 news, queer and gay protesters defied a crackdown on LGBTQ+ rights in Turkey to lead a civil society climate march.

UK news | Two people aged 22 and 23 have died after their car was hit by a BMW being pursued by police. West Yorkshire police said four people had been arrested and appealed for witnesses to come forward.

Air transport | The Trump administration says Friday’s four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that delayed or cancelled thousands of flight stemmed from routine maintenance. The US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, blamed prior presidents and Congress for the stoppage.

Tuesday | The former health and social care secretary Alan Milburn’s long-awaited review into why increasing numbers of young people are falling out of work and education, is expected to be released.

Thursday | German chancellor Friedrich Merz, French president Emmanuel Macron and UK prime minister Andy Burnham will be among around 20 heads of state meeting in Berlin to discuss defence funding for Ukraine, and to establish a unified position on future peace negotiations in its war with Russia.

Friday | This marks last day of the world’s biggest annual climate conference, Cop31, in Turkey, with final negotiations taking place.

sources.title: ‘I saw a picture of a two-year-old girl buried in mud. I knew we had to do something’ – This is climate breakdown
sources.description:
When the floods hit Pakistan he went out to help. Then the water reached his own family. This is Imran Lodhi’s story

Location: Dera Ghazi Khan, Pakistan

Disaster: Pakistan intense monsoon rainfall

Imran Lodhi is a university lecturer with a doctorate in climate change and sustainable development. The 41-year-old was living in Dera Ghazi Khan, a city in south-western Punjab, when floods devastated provinces across Pakistan. Climate change made the monsoon rainfall that caused the floods more intense.
